definitions.gloss: to feel depressed, to be downcast

examples.japanese: {石|いし}が{水|みず}の{底|そこ}に{沈|しず}んだ。
examples.english: The stone sank to the bottom of the water.

examples.japanese: {心|こころ}が{沈|しず}んでいる。
{悪|わる}い{知|し}らせを{聞|き}いて{気持|きも}ちが{沈|しず}んだ。
examples.english: My mood sank after hearing the bad news.

notes:
{沈|しず}む means to sink, go down, or feel depressed. Used for physical sinking and emotional states.

TRANSITIVITY:
- {沈|しず}む (intransitive): to sink
- {沈|しず}める (transitive): to sink something

CONJUGATION (godan む-verb):
- {沈|しず}まない (negative)
- {沈|しず}みます (polite)
- {沈|しず}んだ (past)
- {沈|しず}んで (te-form)

COMMON USES:
- {船|ふね}が{沈|しず}む: the ship sinks
- {太陽|たいよう}が{沈|しず}む: the sun sets
- {気持|きも}ちが{沈|しず}む: to feel depressed
- {心|こころ}が{沈|しず}む: to feel down, be dejected
- {沈|しず}んだ{表情|ひょうじょう}: a dejected expression

RELATED COMPOUNDS:
- {沈没|ちんぼつ}: sinking (of a ship)
- {沈黙|ちんもく}: silence
- {沈殿|ちんでん}: precipitation, sediment

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {落|お}ち{込|こ}む: to get depressed (more colloquial)
- {陥|おちい}る: to fall into (a state)
